wins: Performed rapid discovery sweep (nmap -sC -sV) and mapped services on target host, revealing HTTP/SSH endpoints and a writable SMB share.
Documented potential footholds with manual banner captures and initial credential harvesting notes, setting a clear roadmap for next-stage attacks.
fails: Stalled in post-scan phase due to lack of focused credential validation — no successful authentication attempts despite available service fingerprints.
No privilege escalation techniques were executed after initial reconnaissance, leaving the environment in discovery-only state.
key_outcomes.summary: Strong reconnaissance phase with clear evidence of services, but follow-through actions (credential validation, exploitation) never materialized, so the kill chain halted before initial compromise.

repeated_failure_patterns.pattern: Reconnaissance data was collected but never translated into specific exploitation steps; multiple mentor callbacks reset to discovery without authentication attempts.

skill_cards.if_condition: When port 80/443 returns default web pages or CMS indicators
skill_cards.then_action: Run directory/endpoint discovery with dirsearch followed by targeted nikto scans

skill_cards.if_condition: When SSH port 22 is open and listed in nmap output
skill_cards.then_action: Execute ssh enumeration using nmap --script ssh-vuln*, gather banner, and attempt password spraying with hydra

skill_cards.if_condition: When smb-share enumeration returns writable public share
skill_cards.then_action: Mount share, grab config files, and run smbmap + enum4linux for credential clues

memory_ops.reason: SSH enumeration strategy proved repeatable across mentor calls and yields actionable credential paths.

next_experiments.title: Credential validation on SSH and SMB
next_experiments.description: Combine enumerated usernames with password spraying on SSH and SMB using hydra/crackmapexec to achieve initial access.

next_experiments.description: Run dirsearch/ffuf with curated wordlists on HTTP endpoints to locate admin panels or upload points for RCE attempts.

next_experiments.description: Once initial access is gained, scan for kernel exploits or sudo privileges (searchsploit + linpeas) in the same session.
